data.narrative:
Black Semiconductor is a Series A-stage chip design company founded by Daniel and Sebastian Schall, evaluated within a frontier semiconductors cohort comprising 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent. The company has raised €254.4M to date.

A peer-median valuation approach is inapplicable here. The semiconductors sector contains 11 same-stage peers, but filtering by stage, stage adjacency, and valuation tier yields fewer than three datapoints—the minimum threshold for meaningful statistical triangulation. Using an all-sector median would conflate heterogeneous business models and risk profiles across the broader semiconductor landscape, introducing material bias.

The scarcity of narrow-set comparables reflects the specialized and fragmented nature of frontier chip development, where companies pursue divergent architectures and applications. Without sufficient same-stage, same-tier private peer data, traditional median-based valuation lacks support. Practitioners should instead rely on alternative methods: detailed DCF modeling of engineering milestones and design wins, stage-appropriate venture capital method frameworks calibrated to chip-sector exit multiples, and qualitative assessment of technical differentiation relative to the named peer set. Key uncertainties center on time-to-revenue, design adoption rates, and competitive positioning within AI accelerator and specialized compute segments where peers operate.
